messages:
Alex: Quick bring-up update on Sundial-11b quant experiments (int6/int5) on staging — need quick product + ops recs. TL;DR: int6 ~2.8-3x cheaper per token vs our current float16 baseline, latency slightly better, but we see a consistent quality regression on long-form summarization (~4.6 ROUGE-L pts down on the long-summary slice). Sharing slices and short notes below.

Jordan: Can you paste the eval command + exact slice definition and sampling params? :thinking:

Alex: Eval command:```python eval.py --model sundial-11b --quant int6 --slices summarization_long,qa_long,chat_continuity --top_p 0.92 --temp 0.0 --kv_warm False --shots 2```slice def: summarization_long = docs with >1200 tokens source, target >300 tokens.

Ria: Two quick suspects: (1) KV-cache cold starts with lower-precision kernels amplify autoreg error on long contexts, (2) int5/int6 attention acc loss on long-range attention. Did you try kv_warm True?

Sam: Also verify sampling params — deterministic decoding + quantization sometimes surfaces subtle beam failures. Any changes to decoding?

Alex: We re-ran with kv_warm True and latency improved by ~12% on median but ROUGE-L still ~2.1 pts down (vs 4.6 initial). int5 is worse than int6 (ROUGE drop ~=6.8). PPL delta: long-summ slice ppl +7% (int6), short-summ ppl +1%.

Jordan: If ppl increases only on long slices that's a strong signal quantization noise accumulates with steps. Could try hybrid attention kernels or restrict int5/int6 to shorter contexts.

Ria: Recommendation for product/GTN brief: propose hybrid routing rules — small responses (<512 tokens) -> int5, medium (512-2048) -> int6, long (>2048) -> float16 fallback (or float16 13b alternative). Also recommend prefix-KV caching for first 256 tokens and warmstart on canary to reduce cold-kv noise.

Sam: For ops: run micro-bakeoff with focused priming variants. Variation plan: run 48-run matrix across (int5,int6,float16) x (kv_warm True/False) x (shots 0/2/4) on 1k examples from long-summ slice. Track ROUGE, PPL, token-cost.

Alex: I'll schedule the bakeoff and attach the config. Quick numbers to include in GTN notes: unit cost estimate per 1M tokens: float16 = $X (baseline), int6 ≈ 0.34x cost baseline, int5 ≈ 0.28x cost baseline. Quality callout: int6 median ROUGE delta -2.1 (short), -4.6 (long). We should be explicit about the longform hit.

Jordan: For rollout playbook: start with int6 canary on low-risk routes (summaries <600 tokens, high-volume chat edits), monitor eval hooks + live-quality signal (downstream CTR/undo rate), and keep automatic fallback to float16 if rolling-window ROUGE or synthetic eval drops exceed threshold.

Ria: For the scorecard snapshot to hand to product: include per-slice table (slice name, cost multiplier, ROUGE delta, latency median, suggested routing flag). Example row: "long-summ | 0.34 cost | -4.6 ROUGE-L | +12ms median | fallback to float16". Keep it concise.

ops-bot: canary deploy triggered on staging at 7100001242 :rocket:

Alex: Filing a short scorecard now and will ping once the micro-bakeoff results are in. Thanks all — special callout for GTN: highlight unit-econ win but be explicit that longform summarization needs hybrid routing or fallback.

Sam: sg. let us know when the 48-run matrix completes and we can draft the GTN blurb.
